terms.definition: Quantum objects display wave-like or particle-like behavior depending on the experiment.

formulas.name: de Broglie relation
formulas.when_to_use: To relate a particle's momentum to its matter wavelength.
common_mistakes: Using energy instead of momentum in the denominator.

formulas.name: Planck–Einstein relation
formulas.when_to_use: To calculate the energy carried by a photon from its frequency.
assumptions: The electromagnetic excitation is treated as a photon.
common_mistakes: Mixing ordinary frequency ν with angular frequency ω.

formulas.name: Stefan–Boltzmann law

symbols.M: radiant exitance (emitted power per unit area)

formulas.when_to_use: To find the total thermal power emitted per unit area by an ideal blackbody.

formulas.name: Einstein photoelectric equation
formulas.when_to_use: To determine the maximum kinetic energy of electrons released by incident light.
common_mistakes: Using light intensity instead of frequency to set electron energy

formulas.name: Compton shift relation
formulas.when_to_use: To calculate the wavelength change of a photon scattered by a nearly free electron.
common_mistakes: Using the electron scattering angle instead of the photon angle

formulas.name: Wien displacement law
formulas.when_to_use: To relate a blackbody's temperature to the wavelength where its spectrum peaks.
common_mistakes: Confusing the spectral peak with total emitted power
